Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $OGHO,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C=\{-{C}_{1}\}\cup \{-{C}_{2}\}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ and $-{C}_{2}$ are the same paths as ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284597/assets/b4ce481ac8babb7a3e5707f1ef44417b12e73abe4b4c2143c19b45332642c6d2.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a line segment  from the point $B(0,8)$ to the point $A(-2,8),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a section of the curve $y=-{x}^{3}$ from the point $A(-2,8)$ to the point $O(0,0).$

Given that ${\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=16,$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=xy\,i+y\,j$ and $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the first integral, so we only need to work out the second.

The path ${C}_{2}$ is the section of the curve $y=-{x}^{3}$ from $A$ to $O.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}(t)=t\,i-{t}^{3}\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $-2\le t\le 0.$ Along this curve, we have $x=t$ and $y=-{t}^{3}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t)) & =xy\,i+y\,j \\  & =-{t}^{4}\,i-{t}^{3}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{3})j \\  & =i-3{t}^{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =(-{t}^{4}\,i-{t}^{3}\,j)\cdot (i-3{t}^{2}\,j) \\  & =-{t}^{4}+3{t}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =16+{\int }_{-2}^{0}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =16+{\int }_{-2}^{0}(-{t}^{4}+3{t}^{5})\,\text{d}t \\  & =16+{[-\frac{1}{5}{t}^{5}+\frac{1}{2}{t}^{6}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =16+[0-(-\frac{(-{2}^{5})}{5}+\frac{(-2)^{6}}{2})] \\  & =16-\frac{192}{5} \\  & =-\frac{112}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $F(x,y,z)=4\,i+xz\,j+y\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y+R(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}4\,\text{d}x+xz\,\text{d}y+y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If ${\int }_{C}(y-z)\,\text{d}x+6{z}^{2}\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z$ is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ for some piecewise smooth curve $C,$ then $F(x,y,z)=$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y+R\,\text{d}z
$$

In our case, $P=y-z,Q=6{z}^{2},R=-4y.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}((y-z)\,i+6{z}^{2}\,j-4y\,k)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}(y-z)\,\text{d}x+6{z}^{2}\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $F=(y-z)\,i+6{z}^{2}\,j-4y\,k.$
